ruling: Within 12-18 months of public opposition becoming politically binding, the concession will land on siting/energy/infrastructure and on named consumer-facing product features (deployment cosmetics), not on frontier model releases or capability-training pace — labs will publicly walk back a specific deployment, datacenter, or product tier while training/scaling continues unchanged.
because: Five independently-argued minutes converge on the same structural claim: opposition attaches first to whichever decision surface is locally blockable and politically legible (siting/permitting, a named consumer product, an enterprise agent tier) rather than to the frontier-training pipeline itself, which no minute predicts will slow. The round-2 exchange between ai-pressure, lab-moves, and ai-public-backlash sharpened rather than resolved the dispute over which concession surface moves first (product vs. datacenter), which is the one place real disagreement survived contact.
strongest_minute: lab-moves — its claim explicitly separates the two axes (deployment/siting rationale vs. capability-training pace) and defends that split against the near-identical ai-public-backlash claim by committing to the stronger, falsifiable second half (no lab slows a training run for opposition reasons), which the others leave vaguer.
weakest_minute: overton-tracker — after its round-2 REVISE, its own mechanism argument undercuts its round-1 claim (it admits opposition binds by attaching to one concrete, locally-blockable harm), so the framing-migration claim is doing less independent work than the others and mostly restates the siting mechanism in discourse terms.
shared_assumption: All five minutes assume binding public opposition decomposes into a 'positioning/compliance-lite' pressure that firms can satisfy with a visible but reversible concession, rather than a pressure capable of forcing an actual capability-training slowdown — none argues for this, they just build claims on top of it as a shared premise.
unresolved: Whether the first visible concession will be on the datacenter/siting side (ai-public-backlash, overton-tracker) or the consumer-product side (ai-pressure) — the minutes assert competing sequencing but no minute supplies a mechanism to adjudicate which channel actually moves first.
